title: pkix-chain::Error wraps upstream error types in public surface
description:
pkix-chain::Error wraps five upstream crate error types directly in its public enum variants: pkix_path::Error (Path), pkix_revocation::Error (Revocation), pkix_identity::IdentityError (Identity), pkix_aia::AiaError (Aia), and pkix_path_builder::Error (PathBuild). Each of these is a re-exported type from an upstream crate whose major version is locked into pkix-chain's API surface. A major version bump in any of these five crates forces a major version bump in pkix-chain even if pkix-chain itself has no API change.

This is more concerning for the non-workspace crate pkix_aia::AiaError and pkix_path_builder::Error than for the others, since pkix-path and pkix-revocation are tightly co-versioned within the workspace. However the From impls (e.g. From<pkix_path::Error> for Error, From<pkix_aia::AiaError> for Error) make the upstream type a first-class public API element.

What goes wrong if this stays as-is: Each upstream major bump cascades as a forced major bump of pkix-chain. Pre-1.0 this is free per project policy, but post-1.0 it becomes a coordination headache. The pattern of mapping upstream errors into local stable error enums (like pkix-path does with DerError wrapping der::Error) is already established in the workspace for exactly this reason.
